subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers fail closed on every legacy ownerless session row, even when that may stop a previously working patch workflow after upgrade?
rationale: An ownerless row contains no trustworthy evidence identifying which plugin may mutate it, so choosing unconditional denial versus a separate migration requires explicit security and compatibility intent.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows and leave their management to operators or non-plugin clients, preserving the strongest isolation boundary.

options.title: Require a migration first
options.body: Delay unconditional denial until a doctor or owner-specific migration can safely attribute qualifying legacy rows without runtime adoption.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows and leave their management to operators or non-plugin clients, preserving the strongest isolation boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the clearest available owner of the current session projection and patch architecture where this policy is enforced.
